prompt:
In an experiment to measure $g$, a student times 10 oscillations of a simple pendulum for four lengths $L$.

| $L$ / m | 0.20 | 0.40 | 0.60 | 0.80 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| time for 10 oscillations / s | 9.0 | 12.7 | 15.5 | 17.9 |

For small oscillations $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$.

**(a)** Explain why the student timed 10 oscillations rather than one. **[1]**

**(b)** Determine $g$ using a suitable straight-line graph. **[3]**

**(c)** Each time has an uncertainty of $\pm 0.2\ \text{s}$. Calculate the percentage uncertainty in $T^2$ for $L = 0.20\ \text{m}$. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** The reaction-time uncertainty is shared over 10 periods, so the percentage uncertainty in $T$ is ten times smaller ✓

**(b)** Plot $T^2$ against $L$ ✓ ($T^2$ = 0.81, 1.61, 2.40, 3.20 s²). Gradient $\approx 4.0\ \text{s}^2\,\text{m}^{-1}$ ✓. $g = \tfrac{4\pi^2}{\text{gradient}} \approx 9.9\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ ✓ (accept 9.6 to 10.2)

**(c)** $\tfrac{0.2}{9.0} \times 100 = 2.2\,\%$ for $T$ ✓; doubled for $T^2$: $4.4\,\%$ ✓
